_comment: Feature comparison content for the Feature Comparison sheet. Seeded from Vivek Bhaia_Quote.xlsx (7 Aug 2026). No insurer API supplies this — it is maintained product knowledge, so every value here is a manual entry that ages. Each entry under "plans" is a column: label is the header, provider is one of care/niva/mc/star (or another insurer, which the report drops because the hub cannot quote it), plan is the product the column actually describes, and planMatch holds lowercase fragments used to decide whether that is the plan being quoted.

plans.label: Manipal Cigna Sarvah Param
plans._exactMatchNote: Sarvah has 3 named sub-plan tiers (Pratham/Uttam/Param, confirmed live via a user screenshot of the real results page) with materially different pricing/features — a plain "sarvah" substring match can't tell them apart, the same false-positive class fixed for Care Supreme. Now that electron/mc_result_script.js captures the real selected tier (e.g. "Sarvah Uttam"), exactMatch requires it to equal "plan" exactly instead.

plans.label: MANIPAL CIGNA_Lifetime Plan
plans._exactMatchNote: Lifetime Health has two real variants with materially different pricing (confirmed live: India base premium ~40,085.8 vs Global ~54,070.88 for the same SI/tenure) captured as "Lifetime India"/"Lifetime Global" (see electron/mc_result_script.js) — a plain "lifetime" substring matched both indiscriminately, the same false-positive class fixed for Care Supreme/Sarvah. Neither real captured name equals "Lifetime Health" exactly, so this column now always shows the "features shown are for X, you quoted Y" caveat rather than silently picking one. This is intentional, not a bug: nobody currently knows which variant this column's feature data was transcribed from (even the original source quotation just called it "Lifetime" with no variant noted — see scripts/verify/verify_excel_fixture.js's MC_ADD/50L-1Cr rows). Once someone confirms the variant, set "plan" to the exact real name ("Lifetime India" or "Lifetime Global") to re-enable a real match.

plans.label: Niva Bupa ReAssure 2.0 Bronze
plans._exactMatchNote: Was previously left as a loose planMatch on 'reassure2.0'/'reassure 2.0' — meaning ANY ReAssure 2.0 tier (Silver/Gold/Platinum/Titanium+, which have materially different benefits) silently reported as a confident match to this Bronze-tier data whenever the live per-tier feature lookup (resolveLiveNivaPlan/NIVA_SLUG_KEYWORDS) wasn't available, the same false-positive class already fixed for Care Supreme/Sarvah/Lifetime, except with NO caveat shown at all since the loose match reported matches:true. The real captured plan-name format is now confirmed from two independent sources — electron/niva_result_script.js's own live-DOM comment ('ReAssure2.0 Titanium+', no space before '2.0') and scripts/verify/verify_excel_fixture.js's repeated reference transcription ('Reassure2.0 Bronze', same no-space spacing) — both agree there is no space before "2.0", so "plan" now matches that exactly and exactMatch is safe to enable. planMatch is kept only as the (now unused unless exactMatch is later removed) loose fallback list.

plans.label: Care Supreme
plans._exactMatchNote: Care's real 48-plan catalogue has several other real plans whose names also contain "Care Supreme" as a substring (e.g. "POS Care Supreme Shine", the "Care Supreme - VFM/VFM2/VFM3" family) with materially different SI ladders/add-ons — a plain substring match on planMatch reported a false match for those and silently showed this plan's features under the wrong quote, with no caveat. exactMatch requires the quoted name to equal "plan" exactly (case/whitespace-insensitive) instead.
